name: Orbit AI - Phase 5 - Live dialer call placement (W5.2)

nodes.name: Place call webhook
nodes.notes: 'This is the not-yet-built live-dial engine' every W2.6/W2.7/W3.5 caller reference has been pointing at since those workflows were built - THIS is that caller, real for the first time this pass. Meant to be invoked by the dialer UI/softphone layer (Task: Deals Desk / dialer UI, not part of this n8n library - see workflows/README.md's 'How this library relates to the rest of the repo') right after a rep claims a HopperEntry via hopper-request-next.workflow.json (W3.1). Input: {hopperEntryId, opportunityId, locationId, repId, repSipExtension, phoneNumber, dialerMode}. Preview-mode single-line calling only - see this workflow's own README section on what Power/3-Line dialing (opening multiple simultaneous lines per agent) would need beyond this.

nodes.name: DNC check
nodes.notes: W2.6, called synchronously for real - dnc-check.workflow.json's own notes have said 'meant to be called synchronously by the dialer's own call-placement action before it ever dials' since it was built; this is that call. No overrideRequested/overrideBy passed - an override has to be an explicit rep action with a reason, not something this generic call-placement step silently forwards. neverError:true so a 403 comes back as data to branch on.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, reason: $json.reason || 'Blocked by DNC check.' }) }}

nodes.name: Compliant hours check

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ opportunityId: $('Place call webhook').item.json.body.opportunityId, locationId: $('Place call webhook').item.json.body.locationId }) }}

nodes.notes: W2.7, same 'called synchronously alongside DNC, not instead of it' pairing that workflow's own notes describe. requestedAt omitted - checked against right now, since this is an actual dial happening this instant, not a scheduled/queued one.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, reason: $json.reason || 'Blocked by compliant-hours/consent check.' }) }}

nodes.name: Find local-presence number
nodes.notes: Local presence: queries the account's OWN Telnyx number inventory for one already starting with the callee's area code (assumes phoneNumber is a US 10 or 11-digit number; last-10-digits-minus-4 extracts the 3-digit NPA). This is a real Telnyx API shape (GET /v2/phone_numbers with a filter[phone_number][starts_with] query param), not guessed at random, but UNVERIFIED against a live Telnyx account - confirm the exact filter operator name/nesting once real credentials exist, same caveat as Stripe's rawBody assumption elsewhere in this repo. Building the actual number-buying/pooling side (searching + ordering NEW numbers per area code as the campaign footprint grows) is W5.1's job, not this workflow's - this only picks from whatever the account already owns.

nodes.name: Dial customer leg

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ connection_id: $env.TELNYX_CONNECTION_ID || 'PLACEHOLDER_TELNYX_CONNECTION_ID', to: $('Place call webhook').item.json.body.phoneNumber, from: $('Pick FROM number').item.json.fromNumber, answering_machine_detection: 'premium', webhook_url: ($env.N8N_INSTANCE_URL || '') + '/webhook/telnyx-call-events', client_state: $json.clientState }) }}

nodes.notes: Real Telnyx Call Control v2 API shape (POST /v2/calls, answering_machine_detection:'premium' triggers AMD - Telnyx fires a separate call.machine.detection.ended event with the result once it resolves), not guessed - but UNVERIFIED against a live account, same treatment as every other external integration point in this repo before real credentials exist. This is the AMD half of W5.2.

nodes.name: Dial agent leg

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ connection_id: $env.TELNYX_CONNECTION_ID || 'PLACEHOLDER_TELNYX_CONNECTION_ID', to: 'sip:' + $('Place call webhook').item.json.body.repSipExtension + '@' + ($env.TELNYX_SIP_DOMAIN || 'PLACEHOLDER_TELNYX_SIP_DOMAIN'), from: $('Pick FROM number').item.json.fromNumber, webhook_url: ($env.N8N_INSTANCE_URL || '') + '/webhook/telnyx-call-events', client_state: $json.clientState }) }}

nodes.notes: Dials the rep's own internal SIP extension (Rep.sipExtension, CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md - 'reps get an internal extension on one shared Telnyx SIP trunk/connection, not individual DIDs'). This leg and the customer leg above are dialed in parallel and bridged together once the customer leg's AMD result comes back 'human' - see telnyx-call-events-webhook.workflow.json. No AMD needed on this leg (it's an internal extension, not answered by voicemail).

nodes.name: Write call-control IDs to HopperEntry

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ telnyxCustomerCallControlId: $('Dial customer leg').item.json.data ? $('Dial customer leg').item.json.data.call_control_id : $('Dial customer leg').item.json.call_control_id, telnyxAgentCallControlId: $('Dial agent leg').item.json.data ? $('Dial agent leg').item.json.data.call_control_id : $('Dial agent leg').item.json.call_control_id }) }}

nodes.notes: The correlation write CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md's HopperEntry notes describe - telnyx-call-events-webhook.workflow.json reads telnyxAgentCallControlId back off this same HopperEntry (looked up via hopperEntryId, itself carried in client_state) once the customer leg's AMD result says 'human', so it knows which agent leg to bridge to. Handles both Telnyx's documented {data: {...}} envelope and a bare object, since which shape a real response actually uses isn't confirmed from this sandbox.

nodes.name: Respond: dialing
nodes.notes: Fire-and-forget from here - the dialer UI doesn't wait for the call to actually connect (that's async, delivered via telnyx-call-events-webhook.workflow.json and whatever live-status channel the UI subscribes to, not part of this n8n library - see the Deals Desk/dialer UI task).
